method.surface: Hosted Chrome; direct public DDO Wiki DOM inspection during the preceding read-only audit, plus visual inspection of its linked historical item example.
method.capture_kind: Scoped verbatim DOM text and tooltip HTML, with a separately labeled visual transcription. Excerpts from separate table locations remain separate fields; no joined finished-item quote is invented.
method.observation_clock: Genuine observation intervals bounded by clock__curr_time calls around the preceding browser reads. These grouped access windows are not individual page-load timestamps, source modification times, or the later integration/write time.
method.retention: The preceding read-only audit kept its observations in the browser session. This new file now preserves those actual observations; it does not repair older source packets or change their missing metadata.
method.revision_limit: Each Wiki revision_link is the Permanent link exposed by the inspected article. Historical revision endpoints were not independently reloaded; displayed metadata is not a raw HTTP archive or freshness guarantee.
method.source_authority: DDO Wiki is a community-maintained secondary source. Exact source support does not certify current live-game behavior or all interactions.
method.license: DDO Wiki text: CC BY-SA 2.5; attribution through each article and revision link. The externally hosted historical item image is cited separately, not relicensed as Wiki text.

augment-slots.level_rule_visible_text: Every augment has an associated minimum level requirement to use it. Slotting any augment also increases the slotted item’s minimum level to the level of the slotted augment for as long as that augment is slotted, unless the item's minimum level is already equal or higher.
augment-slots.unique_augments_visible_text: Certain crafting systems use special Augment Slots unique to that system, which cannot accept normal augments. The augments used in these systems, in turn, can only be used in those slots. Examples include Heroic and Legendary Green Steel items from The Vale of Twilight, Slave Lords Crafting items from Against the Slave Lords, and Dinosaur Bone Crafting items from The Isle of Dread.
augment-slots.standard_rule_visible_text:
Most augment bonuses, unless otherwise specified, are an Enhancement Bonus.
Skill augments are a Competence Bonus.
Spell Power augments are an Equipment Bonus.
Named augments are not on the list below; see this list.
augment-slots.scope_limit: The ordinary-color compatibility table supports Colorless in Green/Purple. Standard-augment type rules are not transferred automatically to special Slavers crafting gems.
